reason: The proof uses the defining property of continuity that inverse images of closed sets are closed; the supplied group-theoretic rules are irrelevant.
text:
Since \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous and \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb R\), the inverse image \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). But
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.
